_readme: EVERY piece of text on the site lives in this file. Edit it here, save, done —
you never need to open App.js. `npm start` hot-reloads your changes.
Rules, because JSON is picky:
- Wrap all text in "double quotes". Single quotes are not valid JSON.
- Put a comma between items, but NEVER after the last one in a list or block.
- A literal double quote inside text must be escaped: \"
- No comments allowed. This _readme block is the workaround; the site ignores it.
- Accents and symbols (é — · ≥) can be typed directly. The file is UTF-8.
Adding or removing an entry: copy an existing { ... } block, comma-separate it
from its neighbour, and edit the values. Order in the file = order on the page.
The site is the `prototype` block, top to bottom: the links bar, `name`, `subtitle`, the
`about` paragraphs, then `experience`, `aiWork`, the Essays list and `projects`. It renders
twice. The hidden path in App.js (PREVIEW_PATH) shows all of it, for review, with `aiWork`
above `experience`, the about folded on a phone, and an essay banner under the intro. The front page
at / shows the same block without the Essays, without a row's or a heading's `docs` and
`start` (the technical documents) or a row's `visual`, and without the noindex (src/frontPage.js).
Two things are NOT here, because search engines and link previews read them
before the page runs: the browser-tab title and the description that shows up
when you paste the URL into Slack/LinkedIn. Both are in public/index.html.
Images live in public/images/. A path of "/images/foo.jpg" means the file
public/images/foo.jpg. Project photos are cropped to 4:3 from the centre;
ship them around 480x360.

A row has a `result` line, an optional `short` (the row's text on a phone; the full `text` then opens the fold), an optional `where` (place and date, in italics after `text`; not on a phone), and may have `detail`, `figure`, `docs` and `start`, and a `visual` (an image with `src`, `width`, `height`, `alt` and `caption`, shown in the fold; a GIF also has a still `poster`, shown in its place when reduced motion is asked for, and may have a `video` that a click plays full size). A `figure` has `image`, `alt` and `caption`, and `width` and `height` so nothing shifts. A section may have a `headLink` (one link beside its heading) or `docs` (documents beside it). `essays` is the heading of the list built from content/writing/. `pages` on a PDF is kept but not shown. The PDFs under /docs/notes/ come from the career repo; refresh them with scripts/sync-portfolio-notes.sh, never edit them here.

Draft only, for now: `aboutFold` labels the button that folds the `about` paragraphs on a phone, and `essays.banner` is the small label over the essay banner (which essay and which clip: src/essayBanner.js).
`npm run build` also writes the pages, and the essays, as plain HTML with no
JavaScript needed (scripts/build-static.js), at a second hidden path. It reads
this same file and content/writing/, so there is nothing extra to edit.

prototype._note: The site: the front page at / and, with the Essays and the documents, the hidden PREVIEW_PATH. Every number in a `result` comes from the résumé or a PDF in public/docs. `pages` is the PDF's page count (pdfinfo). A doc with `pending` instead of `href` is a spot waiting for its link; the front page leaves it out.
prototype.name: Ihsan Salari
prototype.subtitle: UWaterloo EE student building AI systems, after co‑ops in signal integrity, datacenter optics and RF for chip manufacturing.
about: I care deeply about the social and environmental impact of my work. With the advent of AI, I believe it is increasingly important for these values to inform decisions, whether on an individual, corporate, or societal level.

Every role I’ve held was in a field new to me, and each time I owned critical deliverables within weeks. At Fab2 I designed a 200 W GaN inverter for RF plasma in a day, achieving first plasma in 3 weeks. At Arista I worked with co‑founder Andy Bechtolsheim on the power architecture for next‑gen high‑density 12.8T XPO and co‑packaged optics. I also ensured signal integrity on PCIe Gen 5 and on the 224G links of leading 102.4T switches.

Six months ago I decided to work on AI projects, because I realized that was likely my future. Now a server of mine runs autonomous AI agents that I talk to over Slack. They build and manage my projects and my learning, from my AI PCB and chip design tools to lesson‑builder.

items.name: Fab2 (Atomic Semi)
items.result: Designed a 200 W Class DE RF inverter in one day and reached first plasma in three weeks. Designed the Rogowski‑coil current sensor for a tens‑of‑MHz RF V‑I probe from a first‑principles model, and characterized the coils on a VNA. Built an end‑to‑end AI PCB design workflow in modular pieces for future use in the team’s existing design process.

items.name: Arista Networks
items.result: Worked with founder Andy Bechtolsheim and senior directors on power architecture definition and PMIC selection for next‑gen co‑packaged optics and 1.6T XPO high‑density pluggable modules. Debugged 224G PAM4 signal integrity on 70 GHz VNAs, which cleared two 102.4T switches for fabrication.

items.name: aiRadar
items.result: Redesigned a 3.5 MHz multi‑stage GaN dc‑dc converter end to end, from topology choice to STM32 firmware and bring‑up.

items.name: University of Waterloo
items.result: Class academic rep and WEEF engineering fund rep. GPA 87%.

items.name: hwde
items.text: an AI PCB engineer, from brief to fabricated board.
items.result: A multi‑stage agentic pipeline in the form of a Claude Code skill takes in a simple brief and produces a PCB design and fab package. Soft orchestration layered with deterministic evals and scripts ensures a pipeline which produces consistent, verifiable, and iteratively improvable outputs, while maintaining a flexible pipeline which evolves as models and harnesses do.

visual.alt: A green motor driver board, PCB-001B Rev A, rendered in 3D: it stands on a black base, tips back and settles flat as the camera circles it.
visual.caption: A motor driver hwde designed, rendered in Blender.

items.name: autobox
items.result: Agent orchestration system which runs on a server and autonomously develops projects and improves its own systems. Communication takes place via Slack, and agents follow thorough work patterns which abstract the user away, enabling autonomous development. Agents share a central library and exchange information via sockets and Slack in order to coordinate development. A PR lander runs reviews and adaptive tests based on edited files before merging. A self‑improvement flow catches failures and evaluates project status against goals to both improve current work and re‑evaluate said goals.

visual.alt: The library the agents share: a list of documents, then a bring-up plan open beside its notes, where a question about a 42 mA reading gets an answer and a proposed change, and a new revision is ready.
visual.caption: The library the agents share, answering a question on a document.

figure.alt: Diagram: a planning session, one per Slack channel, hands work down one of three paths: a subagent, a worker, or a sub-orchestrator.
figure.caption: How a planning session hands out work.

items.name: lesson-builder
items.result: Builds interactive lessons with a chatbot tutor via custom content ingestion, supplemental research, and a thorough review pipeline. Lessons feature multimedia content, from videos to interactive demos, Desmos graphs, and SVGs. The chatbot is built on pedagogical theory and can generate content to better explain concepts. I’ve made 47 lessons spanning 14 topics.

visual.alt: A Slack post announces a lesson on Fourier series; the lesson opens and builds a square wave from sines as harmonics are added, the tutor answers a question beside it, and the lesson ends on quick-check questions.
visual.caption: A lesson, with its tutor docked beside it.

items.name: chip design flow
items.text: AI chip design for digital, analog, and mixed‑signal.
items.result: Three pipelines in the form of Claude Code skills aimed at digital, analog, and mixed‑signal design. These function similarly to hwde’s PCB pipeline, and leverage a combination of deterministic checks and evals, iterative improvement flows based on Karpathy’s autoresearch, and a soft orchestration layer which leverages agent judgement. These skills are being developed and used to design tiles for the Tiny Tapeout GF180 chip.

visual.alt: The layout of a small test chip, an 8-bit counter, in 3D: the camera sweeps low over rows of blue standard cells with gold wiring and grey power rails across them.
visual.caption: An 8-bit counter from the chip flow, its layout in 3D.

figure.alt: Diagram: a task goes to a router, then to agents who do the design, then to scripted gates that send failures back to the agents; once all pass, a person checks it before release.
figure.caption: A design reaches release only through scripted gates and a person.

items.result: C++ that traces charged particles through electric and magnetic fields, with a hybrid RK4 and Euler integrator.
